newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Landsbergis party clear winner in Lithuania vote.
newsitem.headline: Landsbergis party clear winner in Lithuania vote.

text.p: The party of Lithuania's independence leader, Vytautas Landsbergis, was the clear winner of a second round of elections, winning 35 of the 65 seats in contention, official preliminary results showed on Monday.

But Landsbergis, who led the Baltic state's struggle to split from the former Soviet Union, was just one seat short of an overall majority in the 141-seat parliament, having also won 35 seats in the first round.

The Homeland Union had already decided to form a coalition with the Christian Democrats. The preliminary figures showed the Christian Democrats won four seats in Sunday's second round to add to the 11 they gained in the first vote.
This would give the coalition 85 seats and a parliamentary majority.
The former ruling ex-communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) won two seats in the second round to add to the 10 they got in the first round on October 20.
Landsbergis' political comeback in the elections was sweet revenge for his 1992 defeat by the LDLP, who swept him out of office just a year after Lithuania regained its independence from Moscow.
